questions.q: In the Schematic Design Phase of Regular Design Services (Doc 202), what is the primary output provided to the client to establish the project's scale and character?
o: As-Built Drawings
Schematic Design Studies (Site plans, floor plans, and initial elevations)
Technical Specifications
Structural Analysis and Calculations
questions.n: This phase focuses on conceptualizing the project's overall character and spatial relationships through preliminary sketches.

questions.q: During the Design Development Phase, what level of detail is added to the initial schematic drawings?
o: Final construction methods and fabrication details
Bidding instructions for the contractors
Only bubble diagrams and mood boards
Finalized spatial relationships, structural/MEP layouts, and initial material specifications
questions.n: This phase 'fixes' the project's size and character by adding technical system coordination and material choices.

questions.q: What is the specific purpose of the Contract Document Phase in the standard architectural design process?
o: To supervise the daily activities of workers
To select the furniture and interior finishes
To prepare Construction Drawings and Technical Specifications for bidding and permits
To research the site's history
questions.n: This phase produces the legally binding documents used for procurement and construction.

questions.q: In the Bidding or Negotiation Phase, what is the architect's primary duty regarding the selection of the contractor?
o: To assist the owner in evaluating bids, analyzing proposals, and preparing the contract
To hire the contractor directly on behalf of the owner
To personally pay the contractor's downpayment
To act as the guarantor for the contractor's performance
questions.n: The architect acts as a technical advisor to ensure the owner chooses the best-qualified bidder.

questions.q: During the Construction Phase, what is the nature of the architect's 'Supervision' under SPP Doc 202?
o: Supervising only the MEP workers
Periodic Site Visits to check for general compliance and issue Certificates of Payment
Full-time physical presence on the site from 8 AM to 5 PM
No site visits are required after the plans are signed
questions.n: Regular Design Services only require enough visits to ensure the building generally follows the plans.

questions.q: Which service under SPP Doc 203 involves the design of 'Hardscape' elements like walls and paths, and 'Softscape' elements like trees and shrubs?
o: Environmental Site Assessment
Architectural Interiors
Landscape Architectural Design Services
Physical Planning
questions.n: Landscape design focuses on the outdoor environment, integrating natural and man-made elements.

questions.q: Which Specialized Architectural Service involves the layout of interior space, selection of finishes, and lighting design?
o: Space Management Studies
Architectural Interiors (AI)
Acoustic Design
Building Audit
questions.n: AI deals with the detailed design of everything inside the building envelope to enhance function and aesthetic.

questions.q: What is the term for the specialized service that involves the design and layout of Large Land Areas such as industrial estates or subdivisions?
o: Physical Planning
Site Utilization Study
Urban Gardening
Architectural Graphics
questions.n: Physical planning involves the spatial arrangement of infrastructure and land use over large tracts of land.

questions.q: Which specialized service involves the design of a building’s Acoustics or Specialized Lighting systems?
o: Electronic Design
Acoustic Design or Architectural Lighting Layout and Design
Comprehensive Sustainability Analysis
Building Environment Certification
questions.n: These focus on technical performance regarding sound quality and visual illumination in specific spaces.

questions.q: What is the specialized service focused on the preservation, restoration, or reconstruction of historic structures?
o: Forensic Architecture
Heritage Conservation
Comprehensive Development Planning
Structural Audit
questions.n: This service applies specialized knowledge to maintain the historical, cultural, and architectural significance of a building.

questions.q: What is the primary objective of Full-Time Supervision under SPP Doc 204-A?
o: To sell units to potential buyers
To design new revisions on the site
To act as the General Contractor
To ensure work is executed in strict accordance with plans, specs, and quality standards
questions.n: Unlike periodic visits, full-time supervision monitors the daily execution to prevent errors.

questions.q: Who is the person physically deployed to the site by the architect to perform the full-time role under Doc 204-A?
o: The Project Manager
The Construction Inspector (or Resident Architect/Engineer)
The Lead Draftsman
The Building Official
questions.n: This professional stays at the site to observe and record all construction activities.

questions.q: Does the Full-Time Supervisor have the authority to stop work if it is non-compliant with the drawings?
o: No, only the police can stop work
Only if the contractor is not wearing a helmet
Yes, they have absolute authority at all times
Yes, if authorized by the Architect-of-Record (AOR) or the Owner
questions.n: While they monitor, the formal power to stop work must be delegated to them.

questions.q: What is the supervisor’s duty regarding the construction 'Logbook'?
o: To list the names of all the neighbors
To keep it locked in the owner's safe
To write poetry about the design
To maintain a daily record of activities, weather, materials, and problems
questions.n: The logbook is a critical legal and management record of the site's history.

questions.q: How is the compensation for Full-Time Supervision (Doc 204-A) usually handled?
o: It is paid for by the contractor
It is a separate fee, usually on a Salary Basis or 1% to 1.5% of construction cost
It is already included in the 10% design fee
The architect does it for free for big clients
questions.n: Because it requires dedicated on-site personnel, it is billed on top of regular design services.

questions.q: What is the primary responsibility of a Construction Manager (CM) under SPP Doc 204-B?
o: To physically build the foundation
To sign the building permits
To coordinate contractors and ensure project is on time, on budget, and quality-assured
To provide the funds for the project
questions.n: The CM manages the process and coordination of multiple trades and contracts.

questions.q: Does a Construction Manager assume Civil Liability for the structural integrity of the building under Article 1723 of the Civil Code?
o: Yes, they are the head of the project
No, the liability remains with the Architect and Engineers of Record
Only if they are also the architect of the project
Only if the contractor goes bankrupt
questions.n: Managerial liability for the process is distinct from the professional liability for the design's integrity.

questions.q: What management tool is typically used by the Construction Manager to track the project's complex schedule?
o: Social media updates
PERT-CPM (Critical Path Method) or Bar Charts
Handwritten to-do lists
A standard wall calendar
questions.n: These analytical tools help visualize the sequence of tasks and identify potential delays.

questions.q: What is 'Value Engineering' in the context of construction management?
o: Cutting the architect's fee to save money
Designing for the most expensive materials possible
Reviewing design to find cost-effective alternatives that maintain function and quality
Removing the elevator to save on electricity
questions.n: It aims to optimize the value of the project by reducing unnecessary costs without hurting performance.

questions.q: To whom is the Construction Manager (CM) directly responsible and loyal to?
o: The Contractor
The Architect-of-Record
The Owner
The Bank
questions.n: The CM acts as the owner's representative to ensure their interests in time, cost, and quality are protected.

questions.q: Under SPP Doc 205, what are the two main sub-services included in Post-Construction Services?
o: Building and Facilities Administration and Post-Occupancy Evaluation (POE)
Cleaning and Repairing
Selling and Advertising
Demolition and Renovation
questions.n: One focuses on the 'running' of the building; the other focuses on 'learning' from its performance.

questions.q: What is the primary goal of Building and Facilities Administration?
o: To oversee the construction of a new wing
To change the building's design every year
To audit the architect's design fees
To manage daily operations, maintenance, and security to preserve building value
questions.n: It ensures the building remains functional, safe, and financially viable over its lifespan.

questions.q: What is a Post-Occupancy Evaluation (POE) as defined in Doc 205?
o: A study to see if the building meets the needs of its users after move-in
A final walkthrough before the owner pays the contractor
An assessment of the building's taxes
A ceremony to celebrate the building's opening
questions.n: POE uses feedback from occupants to improve future designs and fix current functional issues.

questions.q: In building administration, what is 'Preventive Maintenance'?
o: Scheduling regular inspections and repairs to prevent major failures
Painting the building a new color to prevent it from looking old
Fixing things only when they break completely
Hiring a new cleaning company
questions.n: Proactive maintenance saves money and prevents business interruptions by catching issues early.

questions.q: How is the architect usually compensated for the long-term management services under Doc 205?
o: A one-time bonus at the end of the year
Free use of the building's penthouse
Usually a Fixed Salary or a Percentage of Gross Monthly Income
Payment in shares of the owner's company
questions.n: Management is an ongoing operational task, so the pay is recurring and linked to the building's revenue or staff time.
